question_text: What is the meaning of the date of manufacture "1217" specified on the tyre?

options.text: - manufactured in 12th calendar week of the year 2017
- manufactured in the 12th month (December) of the year 2017
- manufactured on the 1/2/2017

correct_answers.text: - manufactured in 12th calendar week of the year 2017

comment: The date of manufacture indicated on the tire is made up of the manufacturing week and the year of manufacture. So "1217" means: 12th week in the year 2017.

question_text: When should you check the tyre pressure?

options.text: Regularly when the tyres are cool
Directly after a tyre change
Directly after every journey

correct_answers.text: Regularly when the tyres are cool
Directly after a tyre change

comment: You should check the tyre pressure regularly when the tyres are cold and immediately after each tyre change. It is not necessary to check after every journey.

question_text: Your tyre inflation pressure is clearly too low while you driving on public roads. What is the consequence of this?

options.text: There will be a considerable deterioration in the vehicle’s manoeuvrability
The vehicle’s stability will be dangerously reduced when cornering
The level of tyre wear will decrease greatly

correct_answers.text: There will be a considerable deterioration in the vehicle’s manoeuvrability
The vehicle’s stability will be dangerously reduced when cornering

comment: A low tyre pressure results that a larger area of the tyre lies on the asphalt while driving. In addition, the tyre no longer has a round shape and can no longer roll cleanly. If the tyre pressure is significantly too low, the driving stability in curves decreases dangerously and the steering behaviour deteriorates.

question_text: What must you check when regularly inspecting your vehicle’s tyres?

options.text: The air pressure
The tread depth
For external damage

correct_answers.text: The air pressure
The tread depth
For external damage

comment:
You should check your tires at regular intervals. It is important that you control the external state of the tires, make sure that the tires have no external damage and that the legally required minimum profile depth of 1.6 mm is not undercut.
Especially in front of longer journeys or with a higher load, you should make sure to check the tire pressure beforehand.

question_text: What should be noted when changing a tyre using a car jack?

options.text: The car jack may only be applied at the positioning points specified by the vehicle manufacturer
The ground surface must always be stable and skid-resistant
The car jack must always be placed at the mid-point of the vehicle's length

correct_answers.text: The car jack may only be applied at the positioning points specified by the vehicle manufacturer
The ground surface must always be stable and skid-resistant

comment: To attach the jack, the vehicle driver must use the mounting points provided by the manufacturer. A safe surface with anti-slip properties is absolutely necessary for this.

question_text: You have to remove a defective tyre. In what sequence should you proceed?

options.text: Secure the vehicle against rolling away, position the car jack, loosen the wheel nuts, jack up the vehicle, remove the wheel nuts
Secure the vehicle against rolling away, position the car jack, jack up the vehicle, loosen the wheel nuts, remove the wheel nuts
Position the car jack, secure the vehicle against rolling away, loosen the wheel nuts, jack up the vehicle, remove the wheel nuts

correct_answers.text: Secure the vehicle against rolling away, position the car jack, loosen the wheel nuts, jack up the vehicle, remove the wheel nuts

comment: Secure the vehicle against rolling away unintentionally. Put the jack on. Loosen the wheel nuts while the vehicle is still in contact with the ground. Lift with the help of the jack. Unscrew the wheel nuts.

question_text: What does the red symbol on the tyre indicate?

options.text: - is suitable for wintry weather conditions
- also assists driving performance in snowy conditions
- may only be used in combination with snow chains

correct_answers.text: - is suitable for wintry weather conditions
- also assists driving performance in snowy conditions

comment: The symbol means that this tyre is suitable for winter weather conditions and supports the driving characteristics even in snow. Snow chains are not required.

question_text: To what must you pay particular attention when driving with winter tyres?

options.text: - not exceed the permissible maximum speed for these tyres
- not exceed 80 km/h
- only drive as fast as when I am using snow chains

correct_answers.text: - not exceed the permissible maximum speed for these tyres

comment: With winter tyres, you must ensure that you do not exceed the maximum permitted speed for the tyres. You can check this in the speed index.

question_text: Your car is equipped with winter tyres. What is the meaning of the speed label "max. 190 km/h" on your dashboard?

options.text: - may not be exceeded
- applies to wintry road conditions only
- does not apply to dry road conditions

correct_answers.text: - may not be exceeded

comment: You must not exceed the maximum speed of 190 km / h on your winter tires.

question_text: What should you remember when putting winter tyres on your car?

options.text: The tyre inflation pressure should be checked in accordance with the manufacturer's guidelines
You should observe the permissible maximum driving speed for these tyres
The air pressure should be 0.5 bar lower than the manufacturer's guidelines for summer tyres

correct_answers.text: The tyre inflation pressure should be checked in accordance with the manufacturer's guidelines
You should observe the permissible maximum driving speed for these tyres

comment: After installing winter tires, you should check the tire pressure according to the manufacturer's specifications and take into account the maximum permissible speed of the tires. This must not be exceeded.

question_text: This indicator lamp lights up. What could be the cause of this?

options.text: The inflation pressure is too low in one tyre
A recently performed wheel change
A loose wheel nut

correct_answers.text: The inflation pressure is too low in one tyre
A recently performed wheel change

comment:
The tyre pressure indicator light usually shows that the tyre pressure is too low, so check your tyre pressure.
However, a lot can also go wrong with the tyre pressure sensors if you have recently changed your tyres. First check whether you notice anything on the outside of the tyre. If the tyre is visually OK and the indicator light is still on, ask the garage.

question_text: What is the legally prescribed minimum tread depth across the main profile of all the tyres on your car?
comment: The legally regulated minimum profile depth for tyres is 1.6 mm. The main tread features are the grooves in the centre tread areas.

question_text: What are the possible consequences if the wheel nuts are not re-tightened following a tyre change?

options.text: The wheel may become damaged
The wheel can become detached from the vehicle
The tyre can become detached from the hub

correct_answers.text: The wheel may become damaged
The wheel can become detached from the vehicle

comment: If the wheel fasteners are not tightened after a wheel change or this has been neglected due to negligence, the wheel may fall off the vehicle while driving due to vibration. This can cause a serious accident. The wheel cannot come off the rim.
